children: Risk premium for French government bonds, or OATs, is in uncharted territory, leaving bond investors to be driven by sentiment, Citi rates strategist Jamie Searle says in a note. "As such, there is no obvious anchor level, and sentiment is in the driving seat," he says. In the context of sentiment and headline risks likely playing an oversized role, the French budgetary process over the coming weeks and months looks even more fraught, following the scale of the weekend's social unrest, he says. The 10-year OAT-Bund yield spread is trading at 147 basis points shortly after European market opening, according to LSEG. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
